twin.thinCash: Future You: “Our buffer is already thin. Look beyond today's payment and notice which option adds a recurring commitment.”
twin.highStress: Future You: “Money matters, but our stress is becoming expensive too. Which choice creates breathing room we can sustain?”
twin.default: Future You: “We still have room to choose. Compare the recurring cost, the risk it removes and what we value as a family.”

guide.earlyMonths: Quick guide: Emergency funds protect against unplanned costs. Instalments preserve cash today but reduce flexibility in future months.
guide.protectionMonth: Quick guide: A protection gap estimates the financial support dependants may need if income is interrupted. More cover is not automatically better—affordability matters.
guide.surpriseMonth: Quick guide: Compare total cost, useful life and effect on your emergency buffer. Cheap today can cost more later; debt also has a flexibility cost.
guide.default: Quick guide: A sustainable plan balances money, time and wellbeing. Test whether the choice still works after another unexpected expense.

resourceAnswers.rm: Jamie would ask: “What outcome worries you most here—and what monthly commitment would still feel comfortable if another surprise happened?”

rounds.title: Your baby arrives early
rounds.story: Everyone is healthy—but the extra medical care and baby essentials cost S$1,800. How do you handle it?

choices.label: Use the emergency fund
choices.detail: Pay today and keep debt at zero.
choices.reaction: We are debt-free, but our safety net suddenly feels very small.

choices.label: Put it on your credit card
choices.detail: Protect cash now; carry the balance forward.
choices.reaction: Cash is intact, but that bill followed us home.

choices.label: Choose a 6-month instalment plan
choices.reaction: The cost feels manageable—provided nothing else goes wrong.

rounds.title: The daycare decision
rounds.story: Your preferred daycare has one place left. Every option changes more than just your bank balance.

choices.label: Nearby premium daycare
choices.detail: More family time, S$1,250 per month.
choices.reaction: The commute is easy and we get precious evenings back.

choices.label: Affordable daycare farther away
choices.detail: S$850 per month, but a longer commute.
choices.reaction: We save money, though the long days take a little more from us.

choices.label: Extend parental leave
choices.detail: Lose S$1,600 income monthly for three months.
choices.reaction: The budget tightens, but we get a chapter together that will not return.

rounds.title: Your protection check
rounds.story: LifeLens finds a S$420K family protection gap. You can protect more, preserve cash, or postpone the decision.

choices.label: Close the full protection gap
choices.reaction: Knowing the family is protected changes how I sleep at night.

choices.label: Start with essential cover
choices.detail: S$62 monthly; review again next year.
choices.reaction: We covered the biggest risks without over-stretching today.

choices.label: Decide later
choices.detail: Keep every dollar available for now.
choices.reaction: We kept the cash, but the gap is still sitting quietly behind us.

rounds.title: The fridge stops working
rounds.story: Milk, meal prep and groceries are at risk. Your earlier choices determine how painful this feels.

choices.label: Repair it today
choices.reaction: Not glamorous, but the groceries are safe and life keeps moving.

choices.label: Replace it with an efficient model
choices.detail: S$1,400 now; lower future electricity costs.
choices.reaction: It hurt today, but Future Me will thank us every month.

choices.label: Use credit and preserve the buffer
choices.reaction: The fridge is fixed. The payment is now tomorrow's problem.

rounds.title: A promotion comes with a catch
rounds.story: The role adds S$900 monthly, but requires longer hours and more childcare support.

choices.label: Take the promotion
choices.reaction: The future grows faster, though our weekdays feel heavier.

choices.label: Negotiate flexible hours
choices.detail: +S$450 monthly with more time at home.
choices.reaction: Not the biggest raise, but it fits the life we actually want.

choices.label: Stay in the current role
choices.reaction: We chose enough—for now—and that can be a powerful choice too.

rounds.title: Your first family holiday
rounds.story: You made it through the year. Do you celebrate now, protect the buffer, or split the difference?

choices.label: Take the S$2,200 holiday
choices.detail: Spend on a memory you will keep.
choices.reaction: The balance is lower, but this year gave us a memory—not only a spreadsheet.

choices.label: Keep building the safety net
choices.detail: Put the full amount toward resilience.
choices.reaction: We delayed the trip and bought ourselves calm for the next surprise.

choices.label: Choose a nearby S$750 getaway
choices.detail: Celebrate while preserving most of the buffer.
choices.reaction: We found a middle path: a little joy now and some safety later.
